  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:center;margin:0pt;"><b><a id="notes" title="notes" href="#"></a>CATHAY GENERAL BANCORP AND SUBSIDIARIES</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:center;margin:0pt;"><b>NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Unaudited)</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:NatureOfOperations" id="c3187265" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; "><em style="font: inherit;">1.</em> Business</span></i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Cathay General Bancorp (&#8220;Bancorp&#8221;) is the holding company for Cathay Bank (the &#8220;Bank&#8221; and, together, with Bancorp, the &#8220;Company&#8221;), and <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145320278">twelve</span>&#160;limited partnerships investing in affordable housing investments in which the Bank is the sole limited partner. Bancorp also owns <ix:nonFraction id="c145320279" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="Pure" name="caty:PercentageOfSubsidiariesCommonSecuritiesOwnedByParentCompany" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="0">100</ix:nonFraction>% of the common stock of <em style="font: inherit;">five</em> statutory business trusts created for the purpose of issuing capital securities. The Bank was founded in <em style="font: inherit;">1962</em> and offers a wide range of financial services. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, the Bank operates <ix:nonFraction id="c145320282" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_StatementGeographicalAxis-SouthernCaliforniaMember" unitRef="Pure" name="caty:NumberOfBranchLocations" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">24</ix:nonFraction> branches in Southern California, <ix:nonFraction id="c145320283" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_StatementGeographicalAxis-NorthernCaliforniaMember" unitRef="Pure" name="caty:NumberOfBranchLocations" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">17</ix:nonFraction>&#160;branches in Northern California, <ix:nonFraction id="c145320284" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_StatementGeographicalAxis-NY" unitRef="Pure" name="caty:NumberOfBranchLocations" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">9</ix:nonFraction> branches in New York State, <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145320285">four</span> in Washington State, <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145320286">two</span> in Illinois, <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145320287">two</span> in Texas, <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145320288">one</span> in Maryland, Massachusetts, Nevada, and New Jersey, <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145320289">one</span> in Hong Kong, and a representative office in Taipei, Beijing, and Shanghai. Deposit accounts at the Hong Kong branch are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> insured by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (the &#8220;FDIC&#8221;). Current activities of Beijing, Shanghai, and Taipei representative offices are limited to coordinating the transportation of documents to Bank's head office and performing liaison services.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; "><em style="font: inherit;">2.</em> Basis of Presentation and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</span></i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The accompanying unaudited Consolidated Financial Statements have been prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;) for interim financial information and with the instructions to Form <em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-Q and Article <em style="font: inherit;">10</em> of Regulation S-<em style="font: inherit;">X.</em> Accordingly, they do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> include all the information and footnotes required by GAAP for complete financial statements. In the opinion of management, all adjustments (consisting of normal recurring accruals) considered necessary for a fair presentation have been included. Operating results for the interim periods presented are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> necessarily indicative of the results that <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be expected for the year ending <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>. For further information, refer to the audited Consolidated Financial Statements and Notes included in the Company&#8217;s Annual Report on Form <em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-K for the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, filed with the SEC on <em style="font: inherit;"> March&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">2,</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em>&#160;(the <em style="font: inherit;">&#8220;2025</em>&#160;Form <em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-K&#8221;).</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The preparation of the Consolidated Financial Statements in accordance with GAAP requires management of the Company to make estimates and judgments that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities, revenues and expenses, and related disclosures of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of the Consolidated Financial Statements. Actual results could differ from those estimates. The Company expects that the most significant estimate subject to change is the allowance for loan losses.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Certain prior period amounts disclosed have been reclassified to conform to the current presentation with <em style="font: inherit;">no</em>&#160;impact on previously reported net income or stockholders&#8217; equity.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsAndChangesInAccountingPrinciplesTextBlock" id="c3187267" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; "><em style="font: inherit;">3.</em> Recently Issued Accounting Standards Pending Adoption</span></i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><br/> In <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2025, </em>ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2025&#8209;11,</em> &#8220;Interim Reporting (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">270</em>): Narrow&#8209;Scope Improvements&#8221;, was issued. ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">11</em> clarifies and enhances guidance under ASC <em style="font: inherit;">270</em> on interim financial reporting by (i) clarifying the scope of ASC <em style="font: inherit;">270</em> such that it now explicitly applies only to entities that issue complete interim financial statements and related notes under U.S. GAAP, (ii) establishing clear guidance on the form of interim statements and notes, incorporating a comprehensive list of required interim disclosures drawn from across the ASC, and (iii) introducing a requirement to disclose material events and changes occurring after the end of the last annual period that could impact interim results. ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">11</em> will be effective for us for interim periods beginning in <em style="font: inherit;">2028,</em> though early adoption is permitted. ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">11</em> is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expected to have a significant impact on our financial statements.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><br/> In <em style="font: inherit;"> November 2025, </em>ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2025&#8209;09,</em> &#8220;Derivatives and Hedging (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">815</em>): Hedge Accounting Improvements&#8221;, was issued. ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">09</em> amends ASC <em style="font: inherit;">815</em> to align hedge accounting more closely with an entity&#8217;s economic risk management practices. Key amendments include (i) to allow designating a variable price component of a nonfinancial forecasted purchase or sale as the hedged risk, (ii) to allow grouping individual forecasted transactions with similar (<em style="font: inherit;">not</em> identical) risk exposures, (iii) a new model for hedging forecasted interest on variable-rate debt, enabling changes in index or tenor without de-designation, subject to simplifying assumptions, and (iv) additional clarifications related to hedge accounting of nonfinancial components, net written options, and dual-hedge strategies. ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">09</em> will be effective for us beginning in <em style="font: inherit;">2027,</em> though early adoption is permitted. ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">09</em> is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expected to have a significant impact on our financial statements.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> November 2025, </em>ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2025&#8209;08,</em> &#8220;Financial Instruments - Credit Losses (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">326</em>): Purchased Loans&#8221;, was issued. ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">08</em> expands the scope of the &#8220;gross&#8209;up&#8221; method, formerly applicable only to purchased credit&#8209;deteriorated ("PCD") assets, to include acquired non&#8209;PCD loans that meet certain criteria, now referred to as &#8220;purchased seasoned loans&#8221; (PSLs). Under this model, an allowance for expected credit losses is recognized at acquisition, offsetting the loan&#8217;s amortized cost basis, thereby eliminating the day-<em style="font: inherit;">one</em> credit&#8209;loss expense previously required for non&#8209;PCD assets. PSLs are defined as non&#8209;PCD loans acquired either (i) through a business combination, or (ii) purchased more than <em style="font: inherit;">90</em> days after origination when the acquirer was <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> involved in origination. ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">08</em> will be effective for us, on a prospective basis for loans acquired on or after the adoption date, for interim and annual reporting periods beginning in <em style="font: inherit;">2027,</em> though early adoption is permitted. ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">08</em> is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expected to have a significant impact on our financial statements.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> September 2025, </em>ASU <em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">06,</em> &#8220;Intangibles - Goodwill and Other - Internal-Use Software (Subtopic <em style="font: inherit;">350</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">40</em>): Targeted Improvements to the Accounting for Internal-Use Software&#8221;, was issued. ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">06</em> simplifies and modernizes the accounting for internal-use software by removing prescriptive project stage guidance and introducing a new capitalization threshold. Under the revised standard, software development costs are capitalized when management authorizes and commits funding for the project, and it is probable the software will be completed and used as intended. ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">06</em> will be effective in <em style="font: inherit;">2028.</em> ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">06</em> is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expected to have a significant impact on our financial statements.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> November 2024, </em>ASU <em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03,</em> &#8220;Income Statement - Reporting Comprehensive Income - Expense Disaggregation Disclosures (Subtopic <em style="font: inherit;">220</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">40</em>): Disaggregation of Income Statement Expenses&#8221;, was issued. This ASU requires disaggregated disclosure of income statement expenses for public business entities. ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03</em> requires new financial statement disclosures in tabular format, disaggregating information about prescribed categories underlying any relevant income statement expense caption. The prescribed categories include, among other things, employee compensation, depreciation, and intangible asset amortization. Additionally, entities must disclose the total amount of selling expenses and, in annual reporting periods, an entity&#8217;s definition of selling expenses. ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03</em> is effective for us, on a prospective basis, for annual periods beginning in <em style="font: inherit;">2027,</em> and interim periods within fiscal years beginning in <em style="font: inherit;">2028,</em> though early adoption and retrospective application is permitted. ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03</em> is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expected to have a significant impact on our financial statements.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; "><em style="font: inherit;">4.</em> Cash, Cash Equivalents and Restricted Cash</span></i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company manages its cash and cash equivalents based upon the Company&#8217;s operating, investment, and financing activities. Cash and cash equivalents, for the purposes of reporting cash flows, consist of cash and due from banks, short-term investments, and interest-bearing deposits. Cash and due from banks include cash on hand, cash items in transit, cash due from the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco (&#8220;FRBSF&#8221;) and other financial institutions. Short-term investments and interest-bearing deposits include cash placed with other banks with original maturity of <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months or less.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company had average excess balance with FRBSF of $<ix:nonFraction id="c145320372" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="caty:AverageExcessBalancesMaintainedWithFederalReserveBank" scale="9" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">1.11</ix:nonFraction>&#160;billion as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c145320373" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="caty:AverageExcessBalancesMaintainedWithFederalReserveBank" scale="9" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">1.14</ix:nonFraction>&#160;billion as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, the Company had&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c145320374" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:MarginDepositAssets" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">15.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c145320375" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:MarginDepositAssets" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">12.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, respectively, as cash margin that serves as collateral on deposits in a cash margin account for interest rate swaps.&#160;Of the balances held in the cash margin account&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c145320376" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_LegalEntityAxis-BankMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:RestrictedCash" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">3.2</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c145320377" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_LegalEntityAxis-BankMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:RestrictedCash" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">4.3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million&#160;are&#160;restricted as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, respectively.&#160;</p>

format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">159</ix:nonFraction>&#160;AFS securities&#160;in a gross unrealized loss position with <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> credit impairment, consisting primarily of&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c145320398" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_FinancialInstrumentAxis-MortgageBackedSecuritiesMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesAvailableForSaleUnrealizedLossPositionNumberOfPositions" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">138</ix:nonFraction> mortgage-backed securities, <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145320399">ten</span>&#160;U.S. government agency securities,&#160;<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145320400">eight</span>&#160;corporate debt securities,&#160;and&#160;<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145320402">three</span>&#160;collateralized mortgage obligations.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The AFS securities&#160;that were in an unrealized loss position at <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026, </em>were evaluated to determine whether the decline in fair value below the amortized cost basis resulted from a credit loss or other factors. For a discussion of the factors and criteria the Company uses in analyzing securities for impairment related to credit losses, <i>see Note <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> -</i> <i>Summary of Significant Accounting Policies - Allowance for Credit Losses on Available for Sale Securities</i> to the Consolidated Financial Statements in the Company&#8217;s <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>&#160;Form <em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-K.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">During the quarter ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026, </em>the Company recognized an impairment loss of $<ix:nonFraction id="c145320408" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="caty:ImpairmentOnInvestmentSecurities" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">15.7</ix:nonFraction> million on certain available-for-sale investment securities in connection with the Company&#8217;s decision to sell those securities. In <em style="font: inherit;"> April 2026, </em>the Company sold these securities, which had a book value of $<ix:nonFraction id="c145320410" contextRef="d_2026-04-01_2026-04-30_SubsequentEventTypeAxis-SubsequentEventMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AvailableforsaleSecuritiesSoldAtPar" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">210.5</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, resulting in a realized loss of $<ix:nonFraction id="c145320411" contextRef="d_2026-04-01_2026-04-30_SubsequentEventTypeAxis-SubsequentEventMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesAvailableForSaleRealizedLoss" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">15.7</ix:nonFraction> million.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The unrealized losses on the remaining AFS securities were primarily attributable to changes in the yield curve and wider liquidity and credit spreads. The issuers have <em style="font: inherit;">not,</em> to the Company&#8217;s knowledge, exhibited any conditions that would indicate a risk of default. Other than the securities identified for sale, the Company expects to recover the amortized cost basis of its AFS securities and has <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> intent to sell, nor is it more likely than <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> that it will be required to sell, securities in an unrealized loss position before recovery. Accordingly, <ix:nonFraction id="c145320417" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesAvailableForSaleAmortizedCostAllowanceForCreditLossExcludingAccruedInterest" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> allowance for credit losses was recorded on AFS securities as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026, </em>and <ix:nonFraction id="c145320419" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesAvailableForSaleExcludingAccruedInterestAllowanceForCreditLossNotToSellBeforeRecoveryCreditLossPreviouslyRecordedExpenseReversal" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> provision for credit losses was recognized for the quarter.</p>

   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left"><b><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; "><em style="font: inherit;">6.</em> Loans</span></i></b><i> </i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Most of the Company&#8217;s business activities are with clients located in the high-density Asian-populated areas of Southern and Northern California; New York City, New York; Dallas and Houston, Texas; Seattle, Washington; Boston, Massachusetts; Chicago, Illinois; Edison, New Jersey; Rockville, Maryland; and Las Vegas, Nevada. The Company also has loan clients in Hong Kong. The Company has <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> significant&#160;industry concentration, and generally its loans, when secured, are secured by real property or other collateral of the borrowers. The Company generally expects loans to be paid off from the operating profits of the borrowers, from refinancing by other lenders, or through sale by the borrowers of the secured collateral.</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Company evaluates loan modifications made to borrowers experiencing financial difficulty to determine whether the modification results in a new loan under ASC <em style="font: inherit;">310&#8209;20.</em> For modifications that do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> result in a new loan, the Company uses the post&#8209;modification contractual terms, including the post&#8209;modification contractual interest rate, when applying a discounted cash flow method to estimate expected credit losses. Loan modifications made to borrowers experiencing financial difficulty are individually evaluated.&#160;The modification <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>include, but is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> limited to, term extensions, payment delays, interest rate reductions, or a combination of such modifications.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company considers a loan to be in payment default once it is <em style="font: inherit;">90</em> days contractually past due under the modified terms.&#160;The Company closely monitors the performance of modified loans to borrowers experiencing financial difficulty to understand the effectiveness of its modification efforts.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Under the Company&#8217;s internal underwriting policy, an evaluation is performed of the probability that the borrower will be in payment default on any of its debt in the foreseeable future without the modification in order to determine whether a borrower is experiencing financial difficulty.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, there were <ix:nonFraction id="c145320691" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LoansAndLeasesReceivableImpairedCommitmentToLend" scale="6" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> commitments to lend additional funds to borrowers experiencing financial difficulty and whose loans were modified.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">As part of the on-going monitoring of the credit quality of our loan portfolio, the Company utilizes a risk grading matrix to assign a risk grade to each loan. Loans are risk rated based on analysis of the current state of the borrower&#8217;s credit quality. The analysis of credit quality includes a review of sources of repayment, the borrower&#8217;s current financial and liquidity status and other relevant information. The risk rating categories can be generally described by the following grouping for non-homogeneous loans:&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 18pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;"><b>&#9679; </b></p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Pass/Watch </b>&#8211;<b> </b>These loans range from minimal credit risk to higher than average, but still acceptable, credit risk. The loans have sufficient sources of repayment to repay the loans in full, in accordance with all the terms and conditions and remain currently well protected by collateral values.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 20pt; text-indent: -18pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 18pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;"><b>&#9679; </b></p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Special Mention</b> &#8211; Borrower is fundamentally sound, and loan is currently protected but adverse trends are apparent that, if <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> corrected, <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>affect ability to repay. Primary source of loan repayment remains viable but there is increasing reliance on collateral or guarantor support.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 18pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;"><b>&#9679; </b></p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Substandard</b> &#8211; These loans are inadequately protected by current sound net worth, paying capacity, or collateral. Well-defined weaknesses exist that could jeopardize repayment of debt. Loss <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em><em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be imminent, but if weaknesses are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> corrected, there is a good possibility of some loss.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 18pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;"><b>&#9679; </b></p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Doubtful </b>&#8211; The possibility of loss is extremely high, but due to identifiable and important pending events (which <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>strengthen the loan), a loss classification is deferred until the situation is better defined.</p> </td></tr>

   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b>Allowance for Credit Losses</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company has an allowance framework under ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">326</em> for all financial assets measured at amortized cost and certain off-balance sheet credit exposures. The measurement of the allowance for credit losses is based on management&#8217;s best estimate of lifetime expected credit losses inherent in the Company&#8217;s relevant financial assets. The forward-looking concept of current expected credit loss (&#8220;CECL&#8221;) approach requires loss estimates to consider historical experience, current conditions and reasonable and supportable economic forecasts of future events and circumstances.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The ACL&#160;is the combination of the allowance for loan losses and the reserve for unfunded loan commitments. The allowance for loan losses is reported as a reduction of the amortized cost basis of loans, while the reserve for unfunded loan commitments is included within "other liabilities" on the Consolidated Balance Sheets (Unaudited). The amortized cost basis of loans does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> include accrued interest receivable, which is included in "accrued interest receivable" on the Consolidated Balance Sheets. The "Provision for credit losses" on the Consolidated Statements of Operations and Comprehensive Income (Unaudited) is a combination of the provision for loan losses and the provision for unfunded loan commitments.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Management estimates expected credit losses using a combination of historical loss experience, internal credit risk metrics, borrower&#8209;specific information, and external economic forecasts. Historical loss data accounts for portfolio composition, delinquency trends, and other relevant credit indicators. The Company incorporates forward&#8209;looking information by applying reasonable and supportable forecasts of key macroeconomic variables, including GDP, unemployment rates, and real estate market conditions, which are updated regularly and applied consistently across loan portfolios.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <ix:exclude>&#160;</ix:exclude>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Under the CECL methodology, quantitative and qualitative loss factors are applied to our population of loans on a collective pool basis when similar risk characteristics exist.&#160;Loans that do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> share similar risk characteristics with pooled loans include&#160;loans individually evaluated due to credit deterioration, borrower&#8209;specific circumstances and&#160;loan modifications made to borrowers experiencing financial difficulty. Expected credit losses for individually evaluated loans are measured using discounted expected cash flows or, for collateral&#8209;dependent loans, the fair value of collateral less estimated costs to sell.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Quantitative Factors</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Company evaluates expected credit losses for loan pools with similar risk characteristics using quantitative models that incorporate historical loss experience, borrower credit attributes, collateral characteristics, and projected economic conditions. Loan portfolios are segmented into groups such as residential mortgages, commercial and industrial loans, construction loans, and various classes of commercial real estate based on common risk characteristics. The quantitative models estimate lifetime expected credit losses by considering contractual cash flows and&#160;expected prepayments, and the impact of forecasted macroeconomic conditions.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The quantitative framework generally considers the probability that a borrower will default (&#8220;probability of default&#8221; or PD), the expected severity of loss in the event of default (&#8220;loss given default&#8221; or LGD), and the expected exposure at the time of default (&#8220;exposure at default&#8221; or EAD). These components are influenced by historical performance, loan structure, collateral type, and forecasted macroeconomic conditions. The models estimate lifetime expected credit losses by considering contractual cash flows and expected prepayments, and the impact of forecasted economic conditions.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Company applies an <em style="font: inherit;">eight</em> quarter reasonable and supportable forecast period followed by a <em style="font: inherit;">four</em> quarter systematic reversion to long&#8209;term historical loss experience. Multiple economic scenarios <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be considered in developing the forecast, and management applies judgment in determining the weighting of those scenarios.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Expected credit losses are estimated over the contractual term of the loans, adjusted for expected prepayments. The contractual term excludes expected extensions, renewals, and modifications unless such options are included in the original or modified contract and are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> unconditionally cancellable by the Company.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">For certain smaller portfolios with limited historical loss experience, such as SBA loans and, HELOCs, the Company applies a simplified loss&#8209;rate approach that incorporates historical performance, forecasted economic conditions, and reversion to long&#8209;term loss expectations.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Qualitative Factors</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Company applies qualitative adjustments to reflect factors <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> fully captured in the quantitative models, including changes in underwriting practices, borrower concentrations, subportfolio growth, competitive dynamics, regulatory developments, and economic uncertainty. Qualitative adjustments also consider emerging risks, model limitations, and credit trends <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> yet observable in historical data, as well as collateral value considerations for certain loan types.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company&#8217;s CECL methodology requires a significant amount of management judgment in determining the appropriate allowance for credit losses. Several of the steps in the methodology involve judgment and are subjective in nature including, among other things:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Segmenting the loan portfolio</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Determining the amount of loss history to consider</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Evaluating model inputs, assumptions, and data sources</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Assessing expected prepayment behavior</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Selecting and weighting the most appropriate reasonable and supportable economic forecast scenario</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Determining the length and structure of the R&amp;S forecast and reversion periods</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Estimating expected utilization rates on unfunded loan commitments</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Assessing relevant and appropriate qualitative factors.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">In addition, the CECL methodology is dependent on economic forecasts that are inherently imprecise and will change from period to period. Although the allowance for credit losses is considered by management to be appropriate, there can be <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> assurance that it will be sufficient to absorb future losses.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Management believes the allowance for credit losses is appropriate&#160;based on the Company&#8217;s loan portfolio, associated unfunded commitments, credit risk ratings, and other relevant information available.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Individually Evaluated Loans&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">When a loan <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> longer shares similar risk characteristics with other loans, such as in the case of certain nonaccrual loans, the Company estimates the allowance for loan losses on an individual loan basis. Generally, the allowance for loan losses for individually evaluated loans is measured as the difference between the recorded value of the loans and the fair value of the collateral. For loans evaluated individually, the Company uses <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> of <em style="font: inherit;">two</em>&#160;different asset valuation measurement methods: (<em style="font: inherit;">1</em>) the fair value of collateral less costs to sell; or (<em style="font: inherit;">2</em>) the present value of expected future cash flows. If an individually evaluated loan is determined to be collateral dependent, the Company applies the fair value of the collateral less costs to sell method. If an individually evaluated loan is determined <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> to be collateral dependent, the Company uses the present value of future cash flows.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Unfunded Loan Commitments</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Unfunded loan commitments are generally related to providing credit facilities to clients of the Bank and are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> actively traded financial instruments. These unfunded commitments are disclosed as off-balance sheet financial instruments in Note <em style="font: inherit;">10</em>&#160;in the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (Unaudited).</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company estimates expected credit losses over the contractual period in which the Company is exposed to credit risk via a contractual obligation to extend credit, unless that obligation is unconditionally cancellable by the Company, using the same loss factors as used for the allowance for loan losses. The reserve for unfunded loan commitments uses a <em style="font: inherit;">one</em>-year historical usage rate of the unfunded commitments during the contractual life of the commitments. The allowance for unfunded commitments is included in &#8220;other liabilities&#8221; on the Consolidated Balance Sheets. Changes in the allowance for unfunded commitments are included in the provision for credit&#160;losses.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; "><em style="font: inherit;">9.</em> Borrowed Funds</span></i></b></p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i>Borrowings from the Federal Home Loan Bank (</i>&#8220;<i>FHLB</i>&#8221;<i>) </i>&#8211; There were&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c145321966" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:SecuritiesSoldUnderAgreementsToRepurchase" scale="6" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction>&#160;over-night borrowings from the FHLB as&#160;of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>. Our unused borrowing capacity from the FHLB&#160;as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, was&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c145321968" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:FederalHomeLoanBankAdvancesGeneralDebtObligationsDisclosuresAmountOfAvailableUnusedFunds" scale="9" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">7.95</ix:nonFraction>&#160;billion and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c145321969" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:FederalHomeLoanBankAdvancesGeneralDebtObligationsDisclosuresAmountOfAvailableUnusedFunds" scale="9" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">7.89</ix:nonFraction>&#160;billion, respectively, and unpledged securities at <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, was $<ix:nonFraction id="c145321970" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_FinancialInstrumentAxis-FederalHomeLoanBankSecuritiesMember_PledgedStatusAxis-AssetNotPledgedAsCollateralMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesAvailableForSaleExcludingAccruedInterest" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">1.66</ix:nonFraction>&#160;billion and $<ix:nonFraction id="c145321971" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_FinancialInstrumentAxis-FederalHomeLoanBankSecuritiesMember_PledgedStatusAxis-AssetNotPledgedAsCollateralMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesAvailableForSaleExcludingAccruedInterest" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">1.64</ix:nonFraction>&#160;billion, respectively.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i>Long Term Debt</i>&#160;&#8211;<i> </i>The Company established <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> special purpose trusts in <em style="font: inherit;">2003</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">two</em> in <em style="font: inherit;">2007</em> for the purpose of issuing Guaranteed Preferred Beneficial Interests in their Subordinated Debentures to outside investors (&#8220;Capital Securities&#8221;). The proceeds from the issuance of the Capital Securities as well as our purchase of the common stock of the special purpose trusts were invested in Junior Subordinated Notes of the Company (&#8220;Junior Subordinated Notes&#8221;). The trusts exist for the purpose of issuing Capital Securities and investing in Junior Subordinated Notes. Subject to some limitations, payment of distributions out of the monies held by the trusts and payments on liquidation of the trusts, or the redemption of the Capital Securities, are guaranteed by the Company to the extent the trusts have funds on hand at such time. The obligations of the Company under the guarantees and the Junior Subordinated Notes are subordinate and junior in right of payment to all indebtedness of the Company and are structurally subordinated to all liabilities and obligations of the Company&#8217;s subsidiaries. The Company has the right to defer payments of interest on the Junior Subordinated Notes at any time or from time to time for a period of up to <em style="font: inherit;">twenty</em> consecutive quarterly periods with respect to each deferral period. Under the terms of the Junior Subordinated Notes, the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em><em style="font: inherit;">not,</em> with certain exceptions, declare or pay any dividends or distributions on its capital stock or purchase or acquire any of its capital stock if it has deferred payment of interest on any Junior Subordinated Notes.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">At <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, Junior Subordinated Notes totaled&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c145321978" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:JuniorSubordinatedLongTermNotes" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">119.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million with a weighted average interest rate of <ix:nonFraction id="c145321979" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-JuniorSubordinatedDebtMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateEffectivePercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">6.23</ix:nonFraction>%, compared to&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c145321980" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:JuniorSubordinatedLongTermNotes" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">119.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million with a weighted average rate of&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c145321981" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-JuniorSubordinatedDebtMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateEffectivePercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">6.76</ix:nonFraction>% at <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>.    <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; "><em style="font: inherit;">10.</em> Commitments and Contingencies</span></i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">From time to time, Bancorp and its subsidiaries are parties to litigation that arises in the ordinary course of business or otherwise is&#160;incidental to various aspects of its operations. Based upon information available to the Company and its review of any such litigation with counsel, management presently believes that the liability relating to such litigation, if any, would <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be expected to have a material adverse impact on the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial condition, results of operations or liquidity taken as a whole. The outcome of litigation and other legal and regulatory matters is inherently uncertain, however, and it is possible that <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> or more of the legal matters currently pending or threatened against the Company could have a material adverse effect on the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial condition, results of operations or liquidity taken as a whole.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Although&#160;the Company&#160;establishes accruals for legal proceedings when information related to the loss contingencies represented by those matters indicates both that a loss is probable and that the amount of loss can be reasonably estimated,&#160;the Company&#160;does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have accruals for all legal proceedings where there is a risk of loss. In addition, amounts accrued <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em><em style="font: inherit;">not</em> represent the ultimate&#160;loss to&#160;the Company from the legal proceedings in question. Thus, ultimate&#160;losses <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be higher or lower, and possibly significantly so, than the amounts accrued for legal loss contingencies.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">In the normal course of business, the Company from time to time becomes a party to financial instruments with off-balance sheet risk to meet the financing needs of its clients. These financial instruments include commitments to extend credit in the form of loans, or through commercial or standby letters of credit and financial guarantees. These instruments represent varying degrees of exposure to risk in excess of the amounts included in the accompanying Consolidated Balance Sheets. The contractual or notional amount of these instruments indicates a level of activity associated with a particular class of financial instrument and is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> a reflection of the level of expected losses, if any.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company&#8217;s unfunded commitments related to investments in qualified affordable housing and alternative energy partnerships were&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c145322010" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="caty:InvestmentsInAffordableHousingAndAlternativeEnergyPartnerships" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">85.5</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c145322011" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="caty:InvestmentsInAffordableHousingAndAlternativeEnergyPartnerships" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">89.3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, respectively.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Loan Commitments</i> - We enter into contractual commitments to extend credit, normally with fixed expiration dates or termination clauses, at specified rates and for specific purposes. Substantially all of our commitments to extend credit are contingent upon clients maintaining specific credit standards at the time of loan funding. We minimize our exposure to loss under these commitments by subjecting them to credit approval and monitoring procedures. Management assesses the credit risk associated with certain commitments to extend credit in determining the level of the allowance for credit losses.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Standby Letters of Credit</i> - Standby letters of credit are written conditional commitments issued by us to secure the obligations of a client to a <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> party. In the event the client does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> perform in accordance with the terms of an agreement with the <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> party, we would be required to fund the commitment. The maximum potential amount of future payments we could be required to make is represented by the contractual amount of the commitment. If the commitment is funded, we would be entitled to seek reimbursement from the client. Our policies generally require that standby letter of credit arrangements contain security and debt covenants similar to those contained in loan agreements.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; "><em style="font: inherit;">12.</em> Earnings per Share</span></i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Basic earnings per share excludes dilution and is computed by dividing net income available to common stockholders by the weighted-average number of common shares outstanding for the period. Diluted earnings per common share reflects the potential dilution that could occur if securities or other contracts to issue common stock were exercised or converted into common stock and resulted in the issuance of common stock that then shared in earnings. Restricted stock units (&#8220;RSUs&#8221;) with anti-dilutive effect were <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> included in the computation of diluted earnings per share. The following table sets forth earnings per common share calculations:</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:DisclosureOfCompensationRelatedCostsShareBasedPaymentsTextBlock" id="c3187302" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; "><em style="font: inherit;">13.</em> Stock-Based Compensation</span></i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Pursuant to the Company&#8217;s <em style="font: inherit;">2005</em> Incentive Plan, as amended and restated, the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>grant incentive stock options (employees only), non-statutory stock options, common stock awards, restricted stock, RSUs, stock appreciation rights and cash awards to non-employee directors and eligible employees.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">RSUs are generally granted at <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> cost to the recipient. RSUs generally vest ratably over <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145322115">three</span> years or cliff vest after <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145322116">one</span> or <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145322117">three</span> years of continued employment from the date of the grant. While a portion of RSUs <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be time-vesting awards, others <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>vest subject to the attainment of specified performance goals and are referred to as &#8220;performance-based RSUs.&#8221; All RSUs are subject to forfeiture until vested.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <ix:exclude>
    <div class="PGFTR" style="text-align: center; width: 100%">
     <div class="hf-row">
      <div class="hf-cell PGNUM" style="text-align: center; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times New Roman;">
       <em style="font: inherit;">17</em>
      </div>
     </div>
    </div>
    <hr style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; border: none; width: 100%; height: 2px; color: #000000; background-color: #000000"/>
    <div class="PGHDR" style="text-align: left; width: 100%">
     <div class="hf-row">
      <div class="hf-cell TOCLink" style="display: inline-block; text-align: left;">
       <a href="#toc" style="font-weight: initial; font-style: initial; font-variant: initial; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Table of Contents</a>
      </div>
     </div>
    </div>
   </ix:exclude>
   <ix:exclude>&#160;</ix:exclude>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Performance-based RSUs are granted at the target amount of awards. Based on the Company&#8217;s attainment of specified performance goals and consideration of market conditions, the number of shares that vest can be adjusted to a minimum of <ix:nonFraction id="c145322119" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_AwardTypeAxis-PerformanceBasedRestrictedStockUnitsMember_RangeAxis-MinimumMember_VestingAxis-ShareBasedCompensationAwardTrancheOneMember" unitRef="Pure" name="caty:PerformanceBasedRestrictedStockUnitsNumberOfSharesThatMayVestPercentageOfTarget" scale="-2" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">zero</ix:nonFraction> and to a maximum of <ix:nonFraction id="c145322120" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_AwardTypeAxis-PerformanceBasedRestrictedStockUnitsMember_RangeAxis-MaximumMember_VestingAxis-ShareBasedCompensationAwardTrancheOneMember" unitRef="Pure" name="caty:PerformanceBasedRestrictedStockUnitsNumberOfSharesThatMayVestPercentageOfTarget" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="1">150</ix:nonFraction>% of the target. The amount of performance-based RSUs that are eligible to vest is determined at the end of each performance period and is then added together to determine the total number of performance shares that are eligible to vest. Performance-based RSUs generally cliff vest <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145322121">three</span> years from the date of grant.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Compensation costs for the time-based awards are based on the quoted market price of the Company&#8217;s stock at the grant date. Compensation costs associated with performance-based RSUs are based on grant date fair value, which considers both market and performance conditions. Compensation costs of both time-based and performance-based awards are recognized on a straight-line basis from the grant date until the vesting date of each grant.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The following table presents RSU activity during the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfShareBasedCompensationRestrictedStockUnitsAwardActivityTableTextBlock" id="c3187303" escape="true">

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>,&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c145322132" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAvailableForGrant" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">2,812,469</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares were available for future grants under the Company&#8217;s <em style="font: inherit;">2005</em> Incentive Plan, as amended and restated.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; "><em style="font: inherit;">14.</em> Income Taxes </span></i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The effective tax rate for the <em style="font: inherit;">first </em><em style="font: inherit;">three</em>&#160;months of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> was&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c145322175" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:EffectiveIncomeTaxRateContinuingOperations" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">21.0</ix:nonFraction>%&#160;compared to&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c145322176" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-03-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:EffectiveIncomeTaxRateContinuingOperations" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">19.8</ix:nonFraction>%&#160;for the <em style="font: inherit;">first </em><em style="font: inherit;">three</em>&#160;months of <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>. The effective tax rate for the <em style="font: inherit;">first </em><em style="font: inherit;">three</em>&#160;months of <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em>&#160;includes the impact of low-income housing tax credits and for the <em style="font: inherit;">first </em><em style="font: inherit;">three</em>&#160;months of <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>&#160;includes the impact of alternative energy investment and low-income housing tax credits.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company&#8217;s tax returns are open for audit by the Internal Revenue Service back to <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145322186">2023</span>&#160;and by the California Franchise Tax Board and other states where the Company files state tax returns back to <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145322187">2022</span>.&#160;&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">It is reasonably possible that unrecognized tax benefits could change significantly over the next <em style="font: inherit;">twelve</em> months. The Company does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expect that any such changes would have a material impact on its annual effective tax rate.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; "><em style="font: inherit;">15.</em> Fair Value Measurements and Fair Value of Financial Instruments</span></i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company uses fair value to measure certain assets and liabilities on a recurring basis, primarily securities available-for-sale and derivatives. For assets measured at the lower of cost or fair value, the fair value measurement criteria <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>or <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em><em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be met during a reporting period and such measurements are therefore considered &#8220;nonrecurring&#8221; for purposes of disclosing our fair value measurements. Fair value is used on a nonrecurring basis to adjust carrying values for individually evaluated loans and other real estate owned and also to record impairment on certain assets, such as goodwill, CDI, and other long-lived assets.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company used valuation methodologies to measure assets at fair value under ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">820</em> and ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">825,</em> as amended by ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2016</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">01</em> and ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2018</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03,</em> to estimate the fair value of financial instruments <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> recorded at fair value. The fair value of the Company&#8217;s assets and liabilities is classified and disclosed in <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> of the following <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> categories:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> &#8211;&#160;Quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> &#8211;&#160;Observable prices in active markets for similar assets or liabilities; prices for identical or similar assets or liabilities in markets that are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> active; directly observable market inputs for substantially the full term of the asset and liability; market inputs that are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> directly observable but are derived from or corroborated by observable market data.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> &#8211;&#160;Unobservable inputs based on the Company&#8217;s own judgment about the assumptions that a market participant would use.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The classification of assets and liabilities within the hierarchy is based on whether inputs to the valuation methodology used are observable or unobservable, and the significance of those inputs in the fair value measurement. The Company&#8217;s assets and liabilities are classified in their entirety based on the lowest level of input that is significant to their fair value measurements.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Financial assets and liabilities measured at fair value on a recurring basis:</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company uses the following methodologies to measure the fair value of its financial assets and liabilities on a recurring basis:</p>
