   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i>Securities Available-for-Sale</i> <i>and Equity Securities</i> - For certain actively traded agency preferred stocks, mutual funds, U.S. Treasury securities, and other equity securities, the Company measures the fair value based on quoted market prices in active exchange markets at the reporting date, a Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> measurement. The Company also measures securities by using quoted market prices for similar securities or dealer quotes, a Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> measurement. This category generally includes U.S. Government agency securities, U.S. Government sponsored entities, state and municipal securities, mortgage-backed securities (&#8220;MBS&#8221;), collateralized mortgage obligations and corporate bonds.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i>Interest Rate Swaps</i> &#8211; The Company measures the fair value of interest rate swaps using <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> party models with observable market data, a Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> measurement.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i>Currency Option Contracts and Foreign Exchange Contracts</i> - The Company measures the fair value of currency option contracts and foreign exchange contracts based on observable market rates on a recurring basis, a Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> measurement.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Financial assets and liabilities measured at estimated fair value on a non-recurring basis:</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Certain assets or liabilities are required to be measured at estimated fair value on a nonrecurring basis subsequent to initial recognition. Generally, these adjustments are the result of lower-of-cost-or-fair value or other impairment write-downs of individual assets. In determining the estimated fair values during the period, the Company determined that substantially all the changes in estimated fair value were due to declines in market conditions versus instrument specific credit risk.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">For financial assets measured at fair value on a nonrecurring basis that were still reflected in the Consolidated Balance Sheets as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, the following tables set forth the level of valuation assumptions used to determine each adjustment, the carrying value of the related individual assets as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, and the total losses for the periods indicated:</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The significant unobservable (Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em>) inputs used in the fair value measurement of collateral for collateral-dependent individually evaluated loans are primarily based on the appraised value of collateral adjusted by estimated sales cost and commissions. The Company generally obtains new appraisal reports every <em style="font: inherit;">twelve</em> months as appropriate. As the Company&#8217;s primary objective in the event of default would be to monetize the collateral to settle the outstanding balance of the loan, less marketable collateral would receive a larger discount. In the current year, the Company used borrower specific collateral discounts with various discount levels.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The fair value of individually evaluated loans is calculated based on the net realizable fair value of the collateral or the observable market price of the most recent sale or quoted price from loans held for sale. The Company does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> record loans at fair value on a recurring basis. Nonrecurring fair value adjustments to collateral dependent individually evaluated loans are recorded based on the current appraised value of the collateral, management&#8217;s judgment and estimation of value using discounted future cash flows or old appraisals which are then adjusted based on recent market trends, a Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> measurement.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Loans held for sale are recorded at the lower of cost or fair value upon transfer. Loans held for sale <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be measured at fair value on a nonrecurring basis when fair value is less than cost. Fair value is generally determined based on available market data for similar loans and therefore, are classified as Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> measurement.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The significant unobservable inputs (Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em>) used in the fair value measurement of other real estate owned (&#8220;OREO&#8221;) are primarily based on the appraised value of OREO adjusted by estimated sales cost and commissions. The Company applies estimated sales cost and commissions of <ix:nonFraction id="c145322230" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="Pure" name="caty:EstimatedSalesCostAppliedToCollateral" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">5</ix:nonFraction>%&#160;of the collateral value of individually evaluated loans, quoted price, or loan sale price of loans held for sale, and appraised value of OREO.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <ix:exclude>&#160;</ix:exclude>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Fair value is estimated in accordance with ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">825.</em> Fair value estimates are made at specific points in time, based on relevant market information and information about the financial instrument. These estimates do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> reflect any premium or discount that could result from offering for sale at <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> time the Bank&#8217;s entire holdings of a particular financial instrument. Because <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> market exists for a significant portion of the Bank&#8217;s financial instruments, fair value estimates are based on judgments regarding future expected loss experience, current economic conditions, risk characteristics of various financial instruments, and other factors. These estimates are subjective in nature and involve uncertainties and matters of significant judgment and therefore cannot be determined with precision. Changes in assumptions could significantly affect the estimates.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:DerivativeInstrumentsAndHedgingActivitiesDisclosureTextBlock" id="c3187317" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b style="font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;"><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; "><em style="font: inherit;">16.</em> Financial Derivatives</span></i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Company uses derivative instruments to manage exposure to interest rate and foreign currency risk and to assist customers with their risk&#8209;management objectives. Certain derivatives are designated as hedging instruments in qualifying fair value hedge relationships. Other derivatives are economic hedges that do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> qualify for, or the Company has elected <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> to apply, hedge accounting, including derivatives entered into to accommodate customer needs. Derivative instruments are recognized on the Consolidated Balance Sheets at fair value, and the accounting for changes in fair value depends on whether the derivative is designated as a hedging instrument.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Customer Accommodation Derivatives (Economic Hedges)</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Company enters into interest rate and foreign exchange derivative contracts with customers to assist them in managing market risks. For each customer derivative, the Company enters into an offsetting derivative with a third&#8209;party financial institution, including centrally cleared counterparties (&#8220;CCPs&#8221;), resulting in minimal net market risk to the Company. These derivatives are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> designated as accounting hedges and are recorded at fair value, with changes in fair value recognized in earnings.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Certain derivatives cleared through CCPs are subject to daily variation margin. When variation margin is legally characterized as settlement under the CCP&#8217;s rulebook, the daily cash exchanges are accounted for as settlements of the derivative&#8217;s fair value rather than collateral.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, the Company had outstanding customer and offsetting dealer interest rate derivative contracts with a notional amount of&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c145322772" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="caty:DerivativeOutstandingNotionalAmount" scale="9" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">1.13</ix:nonFraction>&#160;billion and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c145322773" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="caty:DerivativeOutstandingNotionalAmount" scale="9" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">1.02</ix:nonFraction>&#160;billion, respectively, fair values of&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c145322774" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DerivativeNotionalAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">20.9</ix:nonFraction> million and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c145322775" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DerivativeNotionalAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">24.0</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively.&#160;As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> customer swap transactions were cleared through a CCP. &#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Company also enters into foreign exchange forward contracts with customers to mitigate the risk of fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates associated with foreign currency deposits or customer&#8209;initiated foreign exchange transactions. These contracts are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> designated as hedging instruments and are recorded at fair value, with changes in fair value recognized in non&#8209;interest income. Period&#8209;end gross positive fair values are recorded in other assets and gross negative fair values are recorded in other liabilities.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The notional amount and fair value of the Company&#8217;s derivative financial instruments <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145322778"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145322792">not</span></span> designated as hedging instruments as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> including interest rate swaps cleared through the CCP, were as follows:</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i>Fair Value Hedges of Individual Loans</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, the Bank&#8217;s outstanding fair value interest rate swap contracts matched to individual fixed-rate commercial real estate loans with a notional amount of $<ix:nonFraction id="c145322780" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-InterestRateContractMember_DerivativeInstrumentsGainLossByHedgingRelationshipAxis-FairValueHedgingMember_HedgingDesignationAxis-DesignatedAsHedgingInstrumentMember" unitRef="USD" name="caty:DerivativeOutstandingNotionalAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">47.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and&#160;a fair value of $<ix:nonFraction id="c145322781" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-InterestRateContractMember_DerivativeInstrumentsGainLossByHedgingRelationshipAxis-FairValueHedgingMember_HedgingDesignationAxis-DesignatedAsHedgingInstrumentMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DerivativeNotionalAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.6</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million.&#160;These swaps are designated as fair value hedges of changes in the fair value of the underlying loans attributable to interest rate movements. The swaps amortize in line with the contractual amortization of the hedged loans and permit prepayments with the same prepayment penalty terms as the related loans. Hedge ineffectiveness for these relationships was <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> significant for the periods presented.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Last</i>&#8209;<i>of</i>&#8209;<i>Layer (Portfolio Layer) Fair Value Hedges</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company has designated&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c145322783" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-LoansReceivableWithPartialTermHedgingDesignationMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:HedgedAssetFairValueHedge" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">577.3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million of notional amount as a last-of layer&#160;fair value hedge of closed pools of fixed-rate loans with an aggregate notional value&#160;of&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c145322784" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-LoansReceivableWithPartialTermHedgingDesignationMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DerivativeNotionalAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">869.3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million&#160;as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>.&#160;The loans included in the closed portfolio are expected to retain sufficient principal such that the hedged layer is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> affected by prepayments, defaults, or other factors under the last&#8209;of&#8209;layer method.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Company uses pay&#8209;fixed, receive <em style="font: inherit;">1&#8209;Month</em> Term SOFR interest rate swaps to hedge the designated last&#8209;of&#8209;layer portion of the loan pools. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026, </em>the hedged last&#8209;of&#8209;layer tranche had a fair value gain basis adjustment of $<ix:nonFraction id="c145322787" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-LoansReceivableWithPartialTermHedgingDesignationMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DerivativeGainOnDerivative" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">2.7</ix:nonFraction> million. These swaps convert the hedged layer into a floating&#8209;rate exposure. The Company&#8217;s objective in these hedging relationships is to reduce exposure to changes in fair value attributable to interest rate movements.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Counterparty Credit Risk</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Derivative contracts expose the Company to the risk that counterparties <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be unable to meet their contractual obligations. The Company manages this risk by transacting with institutional counterparties that have strong credit profiles and by requiring approval from the Bank&#8217;s Board of Directors. Credit exposure is limited to the net favorable fair value and any accrued interest receivable on derivative positions. A significant portion of the Company&#8217;s interest rate swaps are centrally cleared through a derivative clearing organization, which reduces counterparty credit risk.&#160;&#160;</p>
  </ix:nonNumeric>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <div>
    &#160;
  </div>
  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:SupplementalBalanceSheetDisclosuresTextBlock" id="c3187321" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; "><em style="font: inherit;">17.</em> Balance Sheet Offsetting</span></i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Certain financial instruments, including resell and repurchase agreements, securities lending arrangements and derivatives, <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be eligible for offset in the Consolidated Balance Sheets and/or subject to master netting arrangements or similar agreements. The Company&#8217;s securities sold with agreements to repurchase and derivative transactions with upstream financial institution counterparties are generally executed under International Swaps and Derivative Association master agreements that include &#8220;right of set-off&#8221; provisions. In such cases, there is generally a legally enforceable right to offset recognized amounts and there <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be an intention to settle such amounts on a net basis. Nonetheless, the Company does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> generally offset such financial instruments for financial reporting purposes.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The major revenue streams by fee type that are within the scope of ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">606</em> presented in the above table are described in additional detail below:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Fees and Services Charges on Deposit Accounts</span></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Fees and service charges on deposit accounts include charges for analysis, overdraft, cash checking, ATM, and safe deposit activities executed by our deposit clients, as well as interchange income earned through card payment networks for the acceptance of card-based transactions. Fees earned from our deposit clients are governed by contracts that provide for overall custody and access to deposited funds and other related services and can be terminated at will by either party. Fees received from deposit clients for the various deposit activities are recognized as revenue by the Company once the performance obligations are met.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Wealth Management Fees</span></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company employs financial consultants to provide investment planning services for clients including wealth management services, asset allocation strategies, portfolio analysis and monitoring, investment strategies, and risk management strategies. The fees the Company earns are variable and are generally received monthly by the Company. The Company recognizes revenue for the services performed at quarter end based on actual transaction details received from the broker dealer the Company engages.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Practical Expedients and Exemptions</span></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company applies the practical expedient in ASC <em style="font: inherit;">606</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">50</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">14</em> and does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> disclose the value of unsatisfied performance obligations as the Company&#8217;s contracts with clients generally have a term that is less than <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> year, are open-ended with a cancellation period that is less than <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> year or allow the Company to recognize revenue in the amount to which the Company has the right to invoice.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">In addition, given the short-term nature of the contracts, the Company also applies the practical expedient in ASC <em style="font: inherit;">606</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">32</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">18</em> and does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> adjust the consideration from clients for the effects of a significant financing component, if at contract inception the period between when the entity transfers the goods or services and when the client pays for that good or service is <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> year or less.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160; &#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b>Net Interest Income Before Provision for Credit Losses</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Net interest income before provision for credit losses increased&#160;$17.6&#160;million, or 10.0%, to $194.2&#160;million during the&#160;first quarter of 2026, compared to $176.6&#160;million during the same quarter a year ago. The increase was due primarily to a&#160;decrease in interest expense&#160;from deposits, offset by a small decrease&#160;in interest in deposits&#160;with other banks.</p>
  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The net interest margin was&#160;3.43% for&#160;the&#160;first quarter of&#160;2026 compared to&#160;3.25% for the&#160;first quarter of 2025.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">For the&#160;first quarter of 2026, the yield on average interest-earning assets was 5.70%, the cost of funds on average interest-bearing liabilities was&#160;2.99%, and the average cost of interest-bearing deposits was 2.96%. In comparison, for the first quarter of 2025, the yield on average interest-earning assets was 5.89%, the cost of funds on average interest-bearing liabilities was 3.46%, and the average cost of interest-bearing deposits was 3.43%. The decrease in the yield on average interest-bearing liabilities and on average interest-earning assets resulted mainly from lower&#160;interest rates on deposits and lower interest rates on loans and securities, respectively. The net interest spread, defined as the difference between the yield on average interest-earning assets and the cost of funds on average interest-bearing liabilities, was 2.71%&#160;for the quarter ended March 31, 2026, compared to&#160;2.43% for the same quarter a year ago.</p>
  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Non-Interest Income</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Non-interest income, which includes revenues from depository service fees, letters of credit commissions, securities gains (losses), wealth management fees, and other sources of fee income, was $20.7&#160;million for the&#160;first quarter of 2026, an increase of $9.5&#160;million, or 84.8%, compared to&#160;$11.2&#160;million for the&#160;first quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily due to an equity securities&#160;gain of $17.3 million in first quarter of 2026 compared to a loss of $4.2 million in the first quarter of 2025 for a net&#160;increase of $21.5&#160;million gain from equity securities&#160;and&#160;an increase of $1.1&#160;million in derivative fees, offset by an impairment loss of $15.7 million on available-for-sale investment securities in connection with the Company's decision to sell certain impaired securities within that portfolio&#160;when compared to the same quarter a year ago.</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b>Non-Interest Expense</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Non-interest expense increased $1.0&#160;million, or 1.2%, to $86.7&#160;million in the&#160;first quarter of&#160;2026 compared to&#160;$85.7 million in the same quarter a year ago. The increase in non-interest expense in the&#160;first quarter of&#160;2026 was primarily due to&#160;an increase of $3.1&#160;million in salaries and employee benefits, an increase of $1.3&#160;million in other real estate owned expense, offset by a decrease of&#160;$2.3&#160;million in amortization expense of investments in low-income housing and alternative energy partnerships, and $1.0 million in FDIC and State assessments&#160;when compared to the same quarter a year ago. The efficiency ratio was&#160;40.35% in the&#160;first quarter of&#160;2026 compared to&#160;45.60% for the same quarter a year ago.</p>
  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Income Taxes</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The effective tax rate for the&#160;first quarter of&#160;2026 was&#160;21.0%&#160;compared to&#160;19.8%&#160;for the&#160;first quarter of 2025. The effective tax rate includes the impact of low-income housing tax credits in 2025.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Balance Sheet Review</span></i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b>Assets</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Total assets were $24.05&#160;billion as of March 31, 2026, a decrease of $180.9&#160;million, or 0.7%, from&#160;$24.23 billion as of December 31, 2025.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Securities Available-for-Sale</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The carrying value of our securities available-for-sale (&#8220;AFS&#8221;) portfolio was $1.68 billion and $1.66 billion as of March 31, 2026 and December 31, 2025, respectively. The increase in the AFS securities&#160;portfolio consists primarily of a net addition&#160;of $87.8 million in treasury securities was partially offset by the amortization of existing securities during the three months ended March 31, 2026. The increase was partially offset by the amortization of existing securities. AFS&#160;securities represented 7.0%&#160;of total assets as of March 31, 2026, compared to&#160;6.8% of total assets as of December 31, 2025.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The portfolio continues to be concentrated in U.S. government-backed securities, with more than 90% of the AFS investment portfolio invested in U.S. Treasuries and agency mortgage-backed securities issued by Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac with the remainder held in investment-grade securities.&#160;There was no allowance for credit losses provided against the AFS investment securities as of both March 31, 2026 and December 31, 2025. Additionally, there were no credit losses recognized in earnings during the three months ended March 31, 2026, and December 31, 2025.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Company actively manages the investment portfolio in the context of asset/liability objectives, interest rate risk, and market conditions. These evaluations may result in changes to portfolio size, composition, or hedging strategies, including adjustments to the mix of securities classified as AFS.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">During the quarter, the Company recorded a $15.7 million impairment loss related to its decision to sell certain AFS investment securities as part of a portfolio repositioning initiative designed to improve yield while maintaining the portfolio&#8217;s overall duration and credit quality. These securities, with a book value of $210.6 million, were subsequently sold in April 2026, resulting in a realized loss of $15.7 million. The AFS portfolio had an effective duration of 1.9 years at March 31, 2026, compared with 2.0 years at December 31, 2025.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b>Loans</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Gross loans held for investment were $20.17&#160;billion at March 31, 2026, an increase of&#160;$27.4&#160;million, or 0.1%, from&#160;$20.15&#160;billion at December 31, 2025. The increase was primarily due to an increase of $98.0&#160;million, or&#160;3.1%, in commercial loans,&#160;an increase of&#160;$24.0&#160;million, or 0.2%, in commercial real estate loans, and an increase&#160;of $6.7 million, or 3.0% in equity lines, offset by a&#160;decrease of $53.6&#160;million, or 0.9%&#160;in residential mortgage loans,&#160;and a decrease of&#160;$48.5&#160;million, or 14.4%&#160;in real estate construction loans.&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b>Non-performing Assets</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Non-performing assets include loans past due 90&#160;days or more and still accruing interest, non-accrual loans, and OREO. Our policy is to place loans on non-accrual status if interest and/or principal is past due 90&#160;days or more, or in cases where management deems the full collection of principal and interest unlikely. After a loan is placed on non-accrual status, any previously accrued but unpaid interest is reversed and charged against current income and subsequent payments received are generally first applied towards the outstanding principal balance of the loan. Depending on the circumstances, management may elect to continue the accrual of interest on certain past due loans if partial payment is received and/or the loan is well collateralized and in the process of collection. The loan is generally returned to accrual status when the borrower has brought the past due principal and interest payments current and, in the opinion of management, the borrower has demonstrated the ability to make future payments of principal and interest as scheduled.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Management reviews the loan portfolio regularly to seek to identify problem loans. During the ordinary course of business, management may become aware of borrowers that may not be able to meet the contractual requirements of their loan agreements. Such loans generally are placed under closer supervision with consideration given to placing the loans on non-accrual status, the need for an additional allowance for loan losses, and (if appropriate) partial or full charge-off.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The ratio of non-performing assets to total assets was 0.53%&#160;as of March 31, 2026, compared to&#160;0.59% as of December 31, 2025. Total non-performing assets decreased $15.8&#160;million, or&#160;11.0% to $127.9&#160;million at March 31, 2026, compared to&#160;$143.7 million at December 31, 2025, primarily due to a decrease of&#160;$23.4&#160;million, or&#160;20.8%, in non-accrual loans, offset by, an increase&#160;of&#160;$4.5&#160;million, or 449.1%, in accruing loans past due 90 days or more, and an increase of &#160;$3.1 million, or&#160;10.2%, in other real estate owned.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">As a percentage of gross loans, excluding loans held for sale, plus OREO, our non-performing assets were 0.63%&#160;and&#160;0.71% as of&#160;March 31, 2026, and&#160;December 31, 2025, respectively. The non-performing loan portfolio coverage ratio, defined as the allowance for credit losses to non-performing loans, increased to&#160;237.50% as of March 31, 2026, from&#160;183.79% as of December 31, 2025.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Non-accrual Loans</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">As of March 31, 2026, total non-accrual loans were&#160;$89.0 million, a decrease of&#160;$23.4 million, or 20.8%, from&#160;$112.4 million at December 31, 2025, and a&#160;decrease of&#160;$65.6&#160;million, or 42.4%, from&#160;$154.6 million at March 31, 2025. The allowance for the collateral-dependent loans is calculated based on the difference between the outstanding loan balance and the value of the collateral as determined by recent appraisals, sales contracts, or other available market price information, less cost to sell. The allowance for collateral-dependent loans varies from loan to loan based on the collateral coverage of the loan at the time of designation as non-performing. We continue to monitor the collateral coverage of these loans, based on recent appraisals, on a quarterly basis and adjust the allowance accordingly.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="margin: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">For non-accrual loans, the amounts previously charged-off represent 7.7%&#160;of the contractual balances for non-accrual loans as of March 31, 2026, and&#160;14.4% as of December 31, 2025. As of March 31, 2026,&#160;$81.3 million, or 91.4%, of the $89.0&#160;million of non-accrual loans were secured by real estate compared to&#160;$90.9 million, or 80.8%, of the&#160;$112.4 million of non-accrual loans that were secured by real estate as of December 31, 2025. The Bank generally seeks to obtain current appraisals, sales contracts, or other available market price information intended to provide updated factors in evaluating potential loss.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The allowance for loan losses to non-performing loans was&#160;220.95%&#160;as of March 31, 2026, compared to&#160;172.82% as of December 31, 2025. The increase was due primarily to a net&#160;increase in the allowance for loan losses and a decrease in&#160;non-accrual&#160;loans.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b>Loan Interest Reserves</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">In accordance with customary banking practice, construction loans and land development loans generally are originated where interest on the loan is disbursed from pre-established interest reserves included in the total original loan commitment. Our construction loans and land development loans generally include optional renewal terms after the maturity of the initial loan term. New appraisals are obtained prior to extension or renewal of these loans in part to determine the appropriate interest reserve to be established for the new loan term. Loans with interest reserves are generally underwritten to the same criteria, including loan to value and, if applicable, pro forma debt service coverage ratios, as loans without interest reserves. Construction loans with interest reserves are monitored on a periodic basis to gauge progress towards completion. Interest reserves are frozen if it is determined that additional draws would result in a loan to value ratio that exceeds policy maximums based on collateral property type. Our policy limits in this regard are consistent with supervisory limits and range from 50% in the case of land to 85% in the case of one to four family residential construction projects.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">As of March 31, 2026, construction loans of $197.1&#160;million were disbursed with pre-established interest reserves of&#160;$29.1 million, compared to&#160;$225.9 million with pre-established interest reserves of $34.0&#160;million at December 31, 2025.&#160; There were no balances on&#160;construction loans with interest reserves that have been extended with pre-established interest reserves of&#160;$380&#160;thousand at March 31, 2026, compared to a&#160; balance of&#160;&#160;$3.3&#160;million with pre-established interest reserves of $95&#160;thousand&#160;at December 31, 2025.&#160; Land loans of&#160;$18.1 million were disbursed with pre-established interest reserves of&#160;$1.5&#160;million&#160;at March 31, 2026, compared to land loans of $15.3&#160;million with pre-established interest reserves of $1.3&#160;million at December 31, 2025. There were no land loans with interest reserves which have been extended as of March 31, 2026, and December 31, 2025.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">At March 31, 2026, and&#160;December 31, 2025, the Bank had no&#160;loan&#160;on non-accrual status with available interest reserves. There were no&#160;non-accrual residential construction loans, non-accrual non-residential construction loans, and&#160;non-accrual land loans that were originated with pre-established interest reserves as of&#160;March 31, 2026, and December 31, 2025.&#160; While we typically expect loans with interest reserves to be repaid in full according to the original contractual terms, some loans may require one or more extensions beyond the original maturity before full repayment.&#160; Typically, these extensions are required due to construction delays, delays in the sale or lease of the property, or some combination of these two factors.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Loan Concentration</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Most of the Company&#8217;s business activities are with clients located in the high-density Asian-populated areas of Southern and Northern California; New York City, New York; Dallas and Houston, Texas; Seattle, Washington; Boston, Massachusetts; Chicago, Illinois; Edison, New Jersey; Rockville, Maryland; and Las Vegas, Nevada. The Company also has loan clients in Hong Kong. The Company has no significant&#160;industry concentration, and generally our loans are collateralized with real property or other pledged collateral of the borrowers. The Company generally expects loans to be paid off from the operating profits of the borrowers, refinancing by another lender, or through sale by the borrowers of the collateral.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The federal banking regulatory agencies issued final guidance on December&#160;6, 2006, regarding risk management practices for financial institutions with high or increasing concentrations of commercial real estate (&#8220;CRE&#8221;) loans on their balance sheets. The regulatory guidance reiterates the need for sound internal risk management practices for those institutions that have experienced rapid growth in CRE lending, have notable exposure to specific types of CRE, or are approaching or exceeding the supervisory criteria used to evaluate the CRE concentration risk, but the guidance is not to be construed as a limit for CRE exposure. The supervisory criteria are: (1) total reported loans for construction, land development, and other land represent 100% of the institution&#8217;s total risk-based capital, and (2) both total CRE loans represent 300% or more of the institution&#8217;s total risk-based capital and the institution&#8217;s CRE loan portfolio has increased 50% or more within the last thirty-six months. The Bank&#8217;s loans for construction, land development, and other land represented&#160;12% of the Bank&#8217;s total risk-based capital as of March 31, 2026, and&#160;14%&#160;as of&#160;December 31, 2025. Total CRE loans represented&#160;278% of total risk-based capital as of March 31, 2026, and 287%&#160;as of December 31, 2025, which were within the Bank&#8217;s internal limit of 400%, of total capital.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Commercial Real Estate Loans</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The&#160;Company focuses on providing financing to experienced real estate investors and developers who have moderate levels of leverage, many of whom are long-time customers of the Bank. CRE loans totaled $7.64&#160;billion as of March 31, 2026, compared with $7.61&#160;billion as of December 31, 2025, and accounted for 38%&#160;of total loans held-for-investment, not including loans held for sale, as of&#160;March 31, 2026, and December 31, 2025. Interest rates on CRE loans may be fixed or variable. As of March 31, 2026, 21%&#160;and 40%&#160;of our CRE portfolio were&#160;variable rate and hybrid loans in their fixed period, respectively. In comparison, as of December 31, 2025, 21%&#160;and 40%&#160;of our CRE portfolio were&#160;variable rate and hybrid loans in their fixed period, respectively. Loans are underwritten with conservative standards for cash flows, debt service coverage and LTV.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Owner-occupied&#160;properties comprised 25%&#160;of the CRE loans as of&#160;March 31, 2026, and December 31, 2025. The remainder were non-owner-occupied properties, where 50%&#160;or more of the debt service for the loan is typically provided by rental income from an unaffiliated third party.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Commercial-Multifamily Residential Loans</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The&#160;multifamily residential loan portfolio is largely comprised of loans secured by residential properties with five or more units. Multifamily residential loans totaled $2.87&#160;billion as of March 31, 2026, compared with $2.89&#160;billion as of December 31, 2025, and accounted for 14%&#160;of total loans held-for investment, not including loans held for sale,&#160;as of&#160;March 31, 2026, and December 31, 2025. The Company offers a variety of first lien mortgages, including fixed&#160;and variable-rate loans. As of March 31, 2026, 22%&#160;and 40%&#160;of our multifamily residential loan portfolio were&#160;variable rate and hybrid loans in their fixed period, respectively. In comparison, as of December 31, 2025, 24%&#160;and 36%&#160;of our multifamily residential loan portfolio were&#160;variable rate and hybrid loans in their fixed period, respectively.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Commercial-Construction and Land&#160;Loans</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Construction and land loans provide financing for diversified projects by real estate property type. Construction and land loans totaled $360.7&#160;million as of March 31, 2026, compared with $408.0&#160;million as of December 31, 2025, and accounted for 2%&#160;of total loans held-for-investment, not including loans held for sale, as of&#160;March 31, 2026, and December 31, 2025. Construction loan exposure was made up of $289.0&#160;million in outstanding loans, plus $199.8&#160;million in unfunded commitments as of March 31, 2026, compared with $337.6&#160;million in outstanding loans, plus $235.3&#160;million in unfunded commitments as of December 31, 2025. Land loans totaled $71.7&#160;million as of March 31, 2026, compared with $70.4&#160;million as of December 31, 2025.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b>Allowance for Credit Losses</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The following table sets forth information relating to the allowance for loan losses, charge-offs, recoveries, and the reserve for off-balance sheet credit commitments for the periods indicated:</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The increase in the ACL during the quarter was driven primarily by changes in the quantitative component of the reserve. Quantitative reserves increased due to higher modeled lifetime loss estimates, reflecting updates to certain model assumptions intended to better capture the portfolio&#8217;s historical loss experience across economic cycles. These updates resulted in higher expected credit losses across several loan categories.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The qualitative component of the allowance was relatively stable in total; however, qualitative adjustments shifted across portfolios based on management&#8217;s assessment of credit conditions and risk trends. In particular, additional qualitative reserves were applied to certain commercial real estate segments, including office and construction, to reflect market&#8209;specific considerations not fully captured in the model&#8217;s baseline economic forecasts. These increases were offset by reductions in qualitative reserves in other portfolios, resulting in an overall qualitative reserve level that was broadly unchanged from the prior quarter.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The ACL is also influenced by the macroeconomic forecasts used in the Company&#8217;s CECL model. The March 31, 2026 estimate incorporated multiple forward&#8209;looking economic scenarios obtained from a reputable third&#8209;party forecaster. These scenarios reflect a range of potential economic outcomes and include a baseline view of expected conditions, along with more optimistic and more adverse&#160;alternatives. Management applies judgment in determining how these scenarios are incorporated into the allowance estimate, taking into account prevailing economic uncertainty and risks.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">To illustrate the sensitivity of the allowance to changes in economic assumptions, management estimates that applying a 100% weighting to the downside scenario would have increased the ACL by approximately $70.7 million as of March 31, 2026. This analysis is intended to demonstrate the directional impact of more adverse economic conditions and should not be interpreted as a forecast of future allowance levels.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Our methodology, policies and estimates on allowance for credit losses for loans&#160;are described in <i>Item 7 -</i>&#160;<i>Management</i>&#8217;<i>s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations</i>&#160;included in the&#160;2025 Form 10-K. For more information, please also see Note 6&#160;to the Company&#8217;s unaudited Consolidated Financial Statements.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b>Deposits</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Total deposits were $20.68&#160;billion as of March 31, 2026, a decrease of&#160;$218.5&#160;million, or&#160;1.0% from&#160;$20.89 billion as of&#160;December 31, 2025.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company calculates its uninsured deposits based on the methodologies and assumptions used for regulatory reporting. Total uninsured deposits were $10.08&#160;billion as of March 31, 2026, decreasing&#160;approximately&#160;$116.5&#160;million, from&#160;$10.19 billion as of December 31, 2025. Excluding $865.3&#160;million in collateralized deposits, the uninsured and uncollateralized deposits of $9.21&#160;billion was 44.6%&#160;of total deposits as of March 31, 2026. Our unused borrowing capacity from the Federal Home Loan Bank as of March 31, 2026, was $7.95&#160;billion and unpledged securities at March 31, 2026, was $1.66&#160;billion. These sources of available liquidity, including cash and short-term investments, were more than 100% of uninsured and uncollateralized deposits as of March 31, 2026.</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b>FDIC Special Assessment and Uninsured Deposits</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">In 2023, the FDIC issued a final rule implementing a special assessment for certain banks to recover losses to the DIF associated with protecting uninsured depositors of Silicon Valley Bank and Signature Bank upon their failure in March 2023. The Company paid its eighth and final quarterly special assessment during the three months ended March 31, 2026, and its remaining accrual for its estimated special assessment liability is zero as of March 31, 2026. The Company will continue to monitor the estimated loss attributable to the protection of uninsured depositors at Silicon Valley Bank and Signature Bank, which could impact the amount of its accrued liability. In December 2025, the FDIC issued an interim final rule outlining a process for a potential offset to regular quarterly deposit insurance assessments for banks subject to the special assessment if the special assessment amount collected ultimately exceeds losses to the DIF. The FDIC plans to provide additional updates on future offsets or a one-time final shortfall special assessment collection, if any, through future invoices.</p>
  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">In the normal course of business, we enter into various transactions, which, in accordance with GAAP, are not included in our Consolidated Balance Sheets. We enter into these transactions to meet the financing needs of our clients. These transactions include commitments to extend credit and standby letters of credit, which involve, to varying degrees, elements of credit risk and interest rate risk in excess of the amounts recognized in the Consolidated Balance Sheets.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i>Loan Commitments</i> - We enter into contractual commitments to extend credit, normally with fixed expiration dates or termination clauses, at specified rates and for specific purposes. Substantially all of our commitments to extend credit are contingent upon clients maintaining specific credit standards at the time of loan funding. We minimize our exposure to loss under these commitments by subjecting them to credit approval and monitoring procedures. Management assesses the credit risk associated with certain commitments to extend credit in determining the level of the allowance for credit losses.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i>Standby Letters of Credit</i> - Standby letters of credit are written conditional commitments issued by us to secure the obligations of a client to a third party. In the event the client does not perform in accordance with the terms of an agreement with the third party, we would be required to fund the commitment. The maximum potential amount of future payments we could be required to make is represented by the contractual amount of the commitment. If the commitment is funded, we would be entitled to seek reimbursement from the client. Our policies generally require that standby letter of credit arrangements contain security and debt covenants similar to those contained in loan agreements.</p>
  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Capital Resources</span></i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Total equity was&#160;$2.99 billion as of March 31, 2026, an increase of&#160;$61.3 million, from&#160;$2.93 billion as of December 31, 2025, primarily due to net income of&#160;$86.9 million, other comprehensive income&#160;of $10.2&#160;million, stock-based compensation of&#160;$1.6 million, and proceeds from dividend reinvestment of&#160;$0.7 million, offset by&#160;common stock cash dividends of&#160;$25.4 million, and purchase of treasury stock of $12.6&#160;million.&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Capital Adequacy Review</span></i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Management seeks to retain our capital at a level sufficient to support future growth, protect depositors and stockholders, and comply with various regulatory requirements.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

Capital levels required to be considered well capitalized are based upon prompt corrective action regulations, as amended to reflect the changes under the Basel III Capital Rules. See the&#160;2025 Form 10-K for a more detailed discussion of the Basel III Capital Rules.</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Dividend Policy</span></i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Holders of common stock are entitled to dividends as and when declared by our Board of Directors out of funds legally available for the payment of dividends. Although we have historically paid cash dividends on our common stock, we are not required to do so. The Company declared cash dividends per common share of $0.38 and $0.34 for the three months ended&#160;March&#160;31, 2026, and 2025, respectively. The amount of future dividends, if any, will depend on our earnings, financial condition, capital requirements and other factors, and will be determined by our Board of Directors. The terms of our Junior Subordinated Notes also limit our ability to pay dividends. If we are not current in our payment of dividends on our Junior Subordinated Notes, we may not pay dividends on our common stock.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company declared a cash dividend of&#160;$0.38 per share on 66,957,659&#160;shares outstanding on February&#160;26, 2026, for distribution to holders of our common stock on March&#160;9, 2026. The Company paid total cash dividends of $25.4&#160;million in the&#160;first quarter of 2026.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Liquidity</span></i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Liquidity is our ability to maintain sufficient cash flow to meet maturing financial obligations and client credit needs, and to take advantage of investment opportunities as they are presented in the marketplace. Our principal sources of liquidity are growth in deposits, proceeds from the maturity or sale of securities and other financial instruments, repayments from securities and loans, Federal funds purchased, securities sold under agreements to repurchase, and advances from the FHLB. As of March 31, 2026, our average monthly liquidity ratio (defined as net cash plus short-term and marketable securities to net deposits and short-term liabilities) was&#160;13.9% compared to 14.7%&#160;as of December 31, 2025.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Bank is a shareholder of the FHLB, which enables the Bank to have access to lower-cost FHLB financing when necessary. At March 31, 2026, the Bank had an approved credit line with the FHLB of San&#160;Francisco totaling $8.47&#160;billion. There were no total advances from the FHLB of San&#160;Francisco&#160;and there were&#160;$959.5 million in standby letters of credit issued by the FHLB on the Company&#8217;s behalf&#160;as of March 31, 2026. These borrowings bear fixed rates and are secured by the Bank&#8217;s loans. See Note 9&#160;to the Consolidated Financial Statements. At March 31, 2026, the Bank pledged $1.38&#160;billion&#160;of its commercial loans and $1.4&#160;million of securities to the Federal Reserve Bank&#8217;s Discount Window under the Borrower-in-Custody program. The Bank had borrowing capacity of $1.26&#160;billion from the Federal Reserve Bank Discount Window at March 31, 2026.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Liquidity can also be provided through the sale of liquid assets, which may consist of federal funds sold, securities purchased under agreements to resell, and securities available-for-sale. At March 31, 2026, investment securities totaled&#160;$1.68 billion, with $22.5&#160;million pledged as collateral for borrowings and other commitments. The remaining balance was available as additional liquidity or to be pledged as collateral for additional borrowings.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Approximately&#160;99.7% of our time deposits mature within one year or less as of March 31, 2026. Management anticipates that these deposits will reprice lower&#160;as a result of the expected decreases&#160;in the target Fed funds rate expected in 2025. Management anticipates that there may be some outflow of these deposits upon maturity due to the keen competition in the Bank&#8217;s marketplace. However, based on our historical runoff experience, we expect the outflow will not be significant and can be replenished through our normal growth in deposits. As of March 31, 2026, management believes all the above-mentioned sources will provide adequate liquidity during the next twelve months for the Bank to meet its operating needs.</p>
  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The business activities of Bancorp consist primarily of the operation of the Bank and limited activities in other investments. The Bank paid dividends to Bancorp totaling&#160;$45.0 million and&#160;$40.0&#160;million during the&#160;first quarter of&#160;2026 and 2025, respectively.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Critical Accounting Policies</span></i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Our most significant accounting policies are described in Note 1 to the consolidated financial statements included in our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025. Certain of these accounting policies require management to use significant judgment and estimates, which can have a material impact on the carrying value of certain assets and liabilities. We consider these policies to be our critical accounting estimates. The judgment and assumptions made are based upon historical experience, future forecasts, or other factors that management believes to be reasonable under the circumstances. Because of the nature of the judgment and assumptions, actual results could differ from estimates, which could have a material effect on our financial condition and results of operations.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">For additional information regarding critical accounting estimates, see the section titled &#8220;Critical Accounting Policies&#8221; included in Item 7 of our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025. There have been no material changes in the Company&#8217;s application of critical accounting estimates since December 31, 2025.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:small-caps;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><a id="qqd" title="qqd" href="#"></a>Item 3.&#160; QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE DISCLOSURES ABOUT MARKET RISK</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We use a net interest income simulation model to measure the extent of the differences in the behavior of the lending and funding rates to changing interest rates, to project future earnings or market values under alternative interest rate scenarios. Interest rate risk arises primarily through the Company&#8217;s traditional business activities of extending loans and accepting deposits. Many factors, including but not limited to economic, market and financial conditions, movements in interest rates, and consumer preferences, affect the spread between interest earned on assets and interest paid on liabilities. The net interest income simulation model is designed to measure the volatility of net interest income and net portfolio value, defined as net present value of assets and liabilities, under immediate rising or falling interest rate scenarios in 25 basis points increments.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Although the modeling can be helpful in managing interest rate risk, it does require significant assumptions for the projection of loan prepayment rates on mortgage related assets, loan volumes and pricing, and deposit and borrowing volume and pricing, that might prove inaccurate. Because these assumptions are inherently uncertain, the model cannot precisely estimate net interest income, or precisely predict the effect of higher or lower interest rates on net interest income. Actual results will differ from simulated results due to the timing, magnitude, and frequency of interest rate changes, the differences between actual experience and the assumed volume, changes in market conditions, and management strategies, among other factors. The Company monitors its interest rate sensitivity and seeks to reduce the risk of a significant decrease in net interest income caused by a change in interest rates.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">From time to time, Bancorp and its subsidiaries are parties to litigation that arises in the ordinary course of business or otherwise is&#160;incidental to various aspects of its operations. Based upon information available to the Company and its review of any such litigation with counsel, management presently believes that the liability relating to such litigation, if any, would not be expected to have a material adverse impact on the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial condition, results of operations or liquidity taken as a whole. The outcome of litigation and other legal and regulatory matters is inherently uncertain, however, and it is possible that one or more of the legal matters currently pending or threatened against the Company could have a material adverse effect on the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial condition, results of operations or liquidity taken as a whole.</p>

The risk factors disclosed in the 2025&#160;Form 10-K are not the only risks facing the Company. Additional risks and uncertainties, including those not presently known to the Company or that the Company presently believes not to be material, could also materially and adversely affect the Company&#8217;s business, financial condition, and results of operations and stock price.</p>

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><a id="uses" title="uses" href="#"></a><span style="font-variant:small-caps;">Item</span>&#160;2.</b> &#160; &#160;&#160; <b>UNREGISTERED SALES OF EQUITY SECURITIES AND USE OF PROCEEDS.</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" class="finTable" style="font-size: 10pt; width: 100%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; text-indent: 0px;">
